In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the radio emission from star-forming galaxies is dominated by synchrotron emission from cosmic rays, with an efficiency of cosmic-ray production in star-forming regions of about 10-20% of the mechanical energy input into the interstellar medium by stellar feedback processes.

The radio continuum emission of galaxies is dominated by the synchrotron radiation from relativistic electrons spiraling along magnetic field lines in the interstellar medium of the galaxies, with the magnetic fields being generated by dynamo mechanisms.

we have used a large sample of star-forming galaxies to show that the radio continuum-star formation relation is not universal.
we have shown that the radio continuum-star formation relation is a fundamental relation between the star formation rate and the magnetic field in galaxies.
